title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Konbini Drink Label. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every card keeps your pinned mix, the always-visible sidebar, straight pictures and text, and the current words. Three more dealt challengers (a data-sublime barcode field, a sewing-pattern envelope, a degrading broadcast signal) wait in the re-roll pool.

options.label: Konbini Drink Label
options.thesis: The site as one drink label in flavors: a white sleeve, and each project gets its own pure color.
options.viewport: A cobalt can-band sidebar with white label bars; Brew and Buff Life sit as two big flavor panels, red and gold, under a compact intro.
options.risk: Flavor colors can drift toward candy and read young, and a beer project inside a drink-label site may blur into the chrome.

raised.raise: One rake scale governs every angle (three steps from -3 to -8 degrees), and text baselines always stay flat.
Every plate, bar and frame snaps to one shared module, so margins and alignments line up by construction.

options.label: Tokyo Line Sign
options.thesis: The site as a transit line: each project a line color, the sidebar the platform sign.
options.viewport: A navy platform-sign sidebar with line-colored bars; the home page reads as the line, with Brew and Buff Life as its two stops.
options.risk: The most familiar route here: transit styling is a common designer-portfolio move, and real signs lean on station codes and Japanese text the text freeze rules out.

options.label: Glazier's Partition
options.thesis: The site as a glass wall: clear calm panes, and color only where you are.
options.viewport: The sidebar is a glazing elevation whose selected pane floods cobalt; each project sits in its own clear pane.
options.case: Holds clarity, since color reserved for state lets the work lead; loses identification, since a glazier's wall is neither David's world nor a recruiter's.
options.risk: Its native motion is slow light, so the pinned snap and blot need translating, and it can read as Mondrian homage.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: Every page a raked glass slide on a lit goldenrod bed, all set at one type size.
options.viewport: A rack of raked slides with the menu as a tick rail along the rake.
options.case: Loses both: one type size fights the tilted headlines, and a 1971 timetable isn't the reviewers' world.
options.kept: One rake token governs every angle while baselines stay flat.
options.risk: Reads as retro pastiche, and the single type size flattens the work's hierarchy.

options.label: Teletext Magazine
options.thesis: Every page an addressed teletext screen of block-mosaic graphics on black.
options.viewport: A 40-column black screen with double-height headers and the projects as numbered pages.
options.case: Loses both: European broadcast nostalgia most US reviewers won't place, and block graphics compete with the project images.
options.kept: One shared module every element snaps to.
options.risk: Retro novelty, and its rigid grid fights the angled plates.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean designer portfolio, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Your sidebar on a white page; a large intro line, then the two projects as big image tiles.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other student portfolios by design; the mix becomes an add-on.
